protections: P1: the virtual host a request is mapped to (Host / :authority, or whatever name the adapter maps on) must resolve to the same TLS virtual host (SSLHostConfig, including its certificateVerification) that was selected from SNI for the connection; in the pinned code no such check exists anywhere: SNI is used only to choose the SSLEngine (java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SecureNioChannel.java:281, java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SecureNioChannel.java:311, java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/AbstractEndpoint.java:514) and is never exposed to the request layer (java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SSLSupport.java:29-145 has no SNI accessor), while mapping uses the request's serverName (java/org/apache/catalina/connector/CoyoteAdapter.java:674, java/org/apache/catalina/connector/CoyoteAdapter.java:692)

evidence: java/org/apache/coyote/AbstractProcessor.java:297-321 (Host is only syntax-checked and copied into serverName; nothing compares it to the TLS host)
java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SecureNioChannel.java:281 (SNI extracted)
java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SecureNioChannel.java:311 (SNI used only to build the SSLEngine, then dropped)
java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/AbstractEndpoint.java:689-714 (SNI -> SSLHostConfig selection: exact, wildcard, then default)
java/org/apache/catalina/connector/CoyoteAdapter.java:692 (virtual host mapping by serverName)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: HTTP/2 legitimately lets clients reuse one TLS connection for several hosts (connection coalescing), and SSLAuthenticator already warns that CLIENT-CERT and h2 do not mix
evidence: java/org/apache/coyote/http2/Stream.java:493-508 (:authority/host parsed separately into serverName; it does not go through AbstractProcessor.parseHost)
java/org/apache/coyote/http2/Stream.java:511-528 (only compares host against :authority, never against the TLS host)
java/org/apache/coyote/http2/StreamProcessor.java:504-509 (h2 validateRequest is the h2 counterpart of the HTTP/1.1 checks)
java/org/apache/catalina/authenticator/SSLAuthenticator.java:197-206 (existing warning about h2, a plausible reason to treat h2 as out of scope)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: NIO is the default connector, and NIO2 looks like a copy that the same change surely covers
evidence: java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SecureNio2Channel.java:411-451 (separate copy of the SNI extraction and engine creation; a fix that records SNI only in SecureNioChannel.java:281-311 leaves NIO2 with no SNI value)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: reading the SNI from the negotiated SSLSession (ExtendedSSLSession.getRequestedServerNames) works under JSSE, so it looks complete
evidence: java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/openssl/OpenSSLEngine.java:1140 (OpenSSLSession implements plain SSLSession, not ExtendedSSLSession)
java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/openssl/panama/OpenSSLEngine.java:1400 (same for the FFM engine)

No use of ExtendedSSLSession/getRequestedServerNames anywhere under java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net (grep), so an SNI read from the session yields nothing under OpenSSL, and a 'no SNI -> skip' check then silently passes

traps.reason_to_dismiss: with no SNI there is nothing to compare, and clients connecting by IP address legitimately send no SNI
evidence: java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SecureNioChannel.java:284-288 (NOT_PRESENT leaves hostName null)
java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SecureNioChannel.java:291-298 (UNDERFLOW: SNI unparseable within sniParseLimit -> default SSLHostConfig name)
java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/AbstractEndpoint.java:705-708 (null/unknown SNI -> default SSLHostConfig, whose certificateVerification may be weaker than the Host's)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a request with no or an empty Host header (HTTP/1.0) names no virtual host, so there is nothing to compare against SNI
evidence: java/org/apache/coyote/http11/Http11Processor.java:680-682 (Host required only when http11)
java/org/apache/coyote/http11/Http11Processor.java:664-666 (restrictedUserAgents downgrades http11 to false, so Host becomes optional)
java/org/apache/coyote/AbstractProcessor.java:276-284 (absent Host -> populateHost; empty Host -> serverName "")
java/org/apache/coyote/http11/Http11Processor.java:1113-1116 (serverName falls back to the Mapper default host)
java/org/apache/catalina/mapper/Mapper.java:733-734 (unmatched/empty name -> defaultHost, which may be a host that requires client certs)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a plain string-equality check of SNI against Host looks like a complete fix
evidence: java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/TLSClientHelloExtractor.java:429 (SNI is lower-cased; the Host header copied at AbstractProcessor.java:318-321 keeps its case)
java/org/apache/catalina/mapper/Mapper.java:718 (host mapping is case-insensitive)
java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/AbstractEndpoint.java:699-701 (wildcard SSLHostConfig *.example.com serves many names)
java/org/apache/catalina/mapper/Mapper.java:720-727 (wildcard Host mapping)
java/org/apache/coyote/AbstractProcessor.java:300-314 (port stripped from Host before serverName)

Must keep working: SNI a.example.com and Host b.example.com that share one SSLHostConfig, plus a case-only difference; both are legitimate. The correct comparison is on the resolved SSLHostConfig (wrong-object risk if names are compared)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: useIPVHosts and proxyName are opt-in admin settings, and the Host header (which a processor-level check would examine) is still consistent with SNI
evidence: java/org/apache/catalina/connector/CoyoteAdapter.java:667-672 (useIPVHosts maps on the local IP name, not the Host header)
java/org/apache/catalina/connector/CoyoteAdapter.java:585-586 (proxyName replaces serverName after the processor parsed Host)
java/org/apache/catalina/connector/CoyoteAdapter.java:692 (mapping uses that overridden name, so a check of Host vs SNI in Http11Processor/Stream judges a value that is not the mapping key)

masking: T3/T4 only show once the T1 guard exists: the missing SNI producer is invisible until a check consumes it, and then it fails open through the T5 null-SNI branch

conflicts.what: a fail-closed fix for missing SNI (T5) rejects every request on OpenSSL connectors if SNI is read from the session, because OpenSSLSession never supplies it (OpenSSLEngine.java:1140)
rejecting missing SNI breaks clients that connect by IP address and legitimately send no SNI; those must keep reaching the default host with the default SSLHostConfig (AbstractEndpoint.java:705-708)
a strict name-equality rule on h2 streams breaks legitimate connection coalescing across names served by the same SSLHostConfig (wildcard at AbstractEndpoint.java:699-701)

fairness_risks: HTTP/2 connection coalescing across different hosts that share a certificate/SSLHostConfig must keep working (Stream.java:411-445 sets the host per stream on a shared connection)

Clients with no SNI (IP-literal connections) and requests whose SNI was unparseable within sniParseLimit fall back to the default SSLHostConfig (SecureNioChannel.java:284-298) and must keep reaching the default host
A case-only difference between SNI and Host (TLSClientHelloExtractor.java:429 vs Mapper.java:718), and a Host with an explicit port (AbstractProcessor.java:300-314), are legitimate
Wildcard SSLHostConfig (AbstractEndpoint.java:699-701) and wildcard Hosts (Mapper.java:720-727) serve many names under one TLS config
RewriteValve host rewrites re-enter CoyoteAdapter.prepare with an admin-chosen serverName (RewriteValve.java:586-598); an adapter-level guard would reject admin-intended cross-host rewrites
useIPVHosts/proxyName deployments (CoyoteAdapter.java:585-586, 667-672) map on a name the client never sent in SNI

design.why: These four give the widest spread of reasons to dismiss: T1 is the advisory route; T5 (no SNI falls back to the default) is the strongest deepseek-type dismissal; T7 (resolved config versus name, with case and wildcard values that must keep working) is mimo-type; T3/T4 is the producer coverage that only shows once a guard consumes SNI. However, one well-designed guard in CoyoteAdapter.postParseRequest, placed after the mapping name is final (CoyoteAdapter.java:674) and comparing the resolved SSLHostConfig with the one in use, closes T1, T2, T5, T6, T7 and T8 together. Only the producer group stays separate, so there are 2 strictly independent groups, below the 3-5 required. Mark as not usable for stacking unless hidden tests are allowed to require processor-level placement, which would separate T2 and T8 into their own groups.
